name: isFirewallEnabled
definition: CONTESTED -- every implementation returns a boolean, but they measure different things on different populations: a firewall's policy set, management connectivity of firewall devices, an endpoint agent, an intrusion engine's mode, and a cloud resource's network ACL. See conflict.positions.
population: unknown -- firewall policies, firewall devices, endpoint agents, appliance networks or a Key Vault resource, depending on the implementation
evidenceRequiredForTrue: unknown until the meaning is ruled; for the network-firewall reading, a complete read of every managed firewall showing it running and enforcing a policy

conflict.summary: Nine integrations answer this key; eight have category null, which is the only reason the disagreement is not customer-visible today. 11 requirements ask it under Firewall/Firewalls while the one categorised answerer (Meraki) is filed Network Security -- a parent/child relationship the category matcher does not implement (plan A3 note). Wave F unmasks all of it at once, so the meaning has to be settled before the category is.

positions.meaning: The firewall's policy objects are enabled.

positions.source: Tx #1062 (C4), merged to main at acf42245: was 'any one connected', now 'every counted firewall connected'. status.connected is management connectivity, which the file's own header says is the only signal the API offers.

positions.meaning: Answered from the management audit log: an empty log graded PASS. The RTA description claims firmware currency instead.

positions.meaning: A Key Vault's networkAcls.defaultAction is Deny -- a resource network restriction, not a network firewall.
positions.source: RTA description; plan F staging: Azure KeyVault is filed Encryption precisely so that this key does not unmask 11 firewall parameters

proposedResolution.summary: isFirewallEnabled means a network firewall is running and enforcing policy, over every managed firewall. Implementations measuring something else move to keys named for it. Whether management connectivity (Sophos) counts as 'enabled' is a judgement, recorded in the decision.

splitKeys.name: isFirewallEnabled
splitKeys.definition: Every managed network firewall is running and enforcing at least one enabled policy.

splitKeys.name: isIPSEnabled
splitKeys.definition: The intrusion engine runs in prevention mode on every protected network.
wouldTake: Cisco - Meraki - Network Security, if prevention; isIDSEnabled if detection counts

splitKeys.definition: The resource's network access rules deny by default and admit only listed networks.

splitKeys.definition: Percentage of endpoints whose secure-web-gateway agent reports healthy and enabled.

decision.question: Is isFirewallEnabled the network-firewall control only, so that Meraki's intrusion mode, DopeSecurity's endpoint agent and Azure Key Vault's network ACL move to their own keys -- and does Sophos's 'every firewall connected to Central' evidence that the firewall is enabled?
